skill.name: ntm
skill.description: Named Tmux Manager orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini agents in named tmux sessions with dashboards, prompt routing, output capture, and robot-mode automation.
skill.summary: Orchestrate multiple AI coding agents in named tmux sessions.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: The skill is a documentation-only NTM workflow guide, so most backtick-based static findings are Markdown false positives. Real risks remain: remote install scripts are piped into bash, shell integration modifies startup files, command hooks execute local shell commands, and the configuration examples disable agent safety controls.

remediation.issue: Remote install commands execute network content directly through bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash instructions with package manager installs, signed releases, checksums, and a reviewable download step.

remediation.issue: Example agent commands disable approvals, sandboxing, or safety checks.
remediation.suggestion: Show safe default agent commands first and move unrestricted modes to a clearly isolated disposable-environment warning.

remediation.issue: Shell initialization writes eval output into ~/.zshrc.
remediation.suggestion: Document what ntm init emits, require explicit user review before editing shell startup files, and provide uninstall instructions.

remediation.issue: Command hooks can run arbitrary shell commands during NTM events.
remediation.suggestion: Add allowlisting, quoting guidance, dry-run output, and warnings that hooks should never process untrusted values as shell code.

remediation.issue: Hook examples can write prompt content into hidden local logs.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users that prompts and pane output may contain secrets, and recommend explicit log paths, permissions, and retention limits.

content.value_statement: Managing several AI coding agents across terminals is hard to track and coordinate. NTM centralizes Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini agents inside named tmux sessions with routing, dashboards, and automation.
actual_capabilities: Creates named tmux sessions with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or empty panes.
Sends prompts to selected agent groups or all panes in a session.
Provides a command palette and visual dashboard for session navigation.
Captures, filters, saves, and compares pane output from running agents.
Exposes robot-mode commands for status, spawning, messaging, and work assignment.
Documents integrations with Agent Mail, BV, CASS, and context rotation workflows.
limitations: Requires the external NTM CLI, tmux, and configured agent CLIs to be installed.
The skill file documents workflows but does not include the Go implementation.
Several integrations depend on separate Flywheel tools that are not bundled here.
Automation can amplify risky prompts, so commands and agent permissions need review.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Coding Agents
use_cases.description: Run Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini in one tmux session while assigning different implementation, review, and testing tasks.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long Agent Sessions
use_cases.description: Use dashboards, activity checks, context indicators, and output capture to supervise multi-hour agent work from one terminal.

use_cases.title: Automate Agent Operations
use_cases.description: Use robot-mode status, spawn, send, and assignment commands from scripts or AI controllers that need machine-readable session state.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent Session
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NTM to create a session named api-review with one Claude Code pane and one Codex pane. Explain the expected pane layout and next command.

prompt_templates.title: Route Work by Agent Role
prompt_templates.scenario: Assign separate tasks to different AI agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an NTM workflow where Claude Code designs the change, Codex implements it, and Gemini reviews documentation. Include safe prompt wording.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Monitoring Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to inspect health, activity, context usage, and output for an NTM session named release-fix. Include when to intervene manually.

prompt_templates.title: Design Robot-Mode Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced orchestration from another automation layer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a robot-mode control loop for NTM that checks session state, assigns work, sends prompts, and stops before dangerous commands run.

output_examples.input: Create a session with two Claude Code agents and one Codex agent for a backend refactor.
